answer: A threshold ring signature proves that at least t members of a group signed, without revealing which ones, and the dune of the construction hides the signers inside a larger anonymity set. The karst structure means a verifier knows a real quorum acted but cannot tell members apart, so Sybil identities cannot amplify their voice: each real person still contributes only one ring slot. Forging requires corrupting a threshold of distinct members, and the timber of the ring keeps membership itself auditable.
